para.name: Jack, Rigid Rack and Lift Support Locations

step1.ptxt: Precautions when Jacking Up or Lifting Up the Vehicle

step2.ptxt: As a rule, the vehicle should be nearly unladen; never jack up or lift up the vehicle with heavy objects loaded.

When heavy components such as the engine or transmission are removed, the center of gravity of the vehicle shifts. Therefore, either load balance weights so that they cannot roll, or support the jack support points with a transmission jack, etc.
Make sure that jacks, rigid racks, support blocks, attachments, etc. securely support the specified positions.
Never jack up or lift up a vehicle that exceeds the capacity of the jack or lift.

step1.ptxt: Support Positions when Jacking Up or Lifting Up the Vehicle
Precautions when Using Jack and Rigid Racks

step2.ptxt: Always work on a level surface and use wheel chocks.
Use rigid racks with rubber attachments as shown in the illustration.
Securely support the specified position with the center of the jack saddle.
Securely support the specified positions with the rigid racks.
When jacking up the front wheels, release the parking brake and place chocks only behind the rear wheels. When jacking up the rear wheels, place chocks only in front of the front wheels.
When jacking up only the front or rear wheels, place chocks both in front of and behind the wheels that are on the ground.

atten3.ptxt: Do not work on or leave the vehicle supported only by a jack; always support it with rigid racks.

step2.ptxt: When lowering the vehicle from a state in which only the front wheels are jacked up, release the parking brake and place chocks only in front of the rear wheels. When lowering the vehicle from a state in which only the rear wheels are jacked up, place chocks only behind the front wheels.
Follow the lift instruction manual and work safely.

atten3.ptxt: If the lift post positions are significantly offset from the vehicle's center of gravity, the vehicle may become very unstable or the vehicle under cover, etc. may be damaged.

step2.ptxt: Use plate lift attachments.
When lifting up the vehicle with a plate lift, check that the vehicle's center of gravity is within the allowable center of gravity range of the lift platform.

atten3.ptxt: If the vehicle's center of gravity is outside the allowable center of gravity range of the lift, the vehicle may sway when raised or lowered.

atten4.ptxt: If the allowable center of gravity range is unknown, contact the lift manufacturer.

step2.ptxt: Always drive the vehicle onto the specified position.

entry.ptxt: Drive onto the center of the lift.

item.ptxt: Align the end of the plate cushion rubber with the end of the bottom surface of the attachment. (Part A)
Align the end of the top surface of the attachment with the front notch of the front rigid rack support position, adjusting it so that it does not contact the rocker molding. (Part B)
Align the rear attachments with the positions shown in the illustration. (Part C)

step2.ptxt: Lift up the vehicle until the tires are slightly off the ground, rock the vehicle and check that it is stable.

step1.ptxt: Precautions when Using Swing Arm Lift

step2.ptxt: Follow the lift instruction manual and work safely.
Use lift pads with rubber attachments as shown in the illustration.
Drive the vehicle onto the lift so that the center of the lift and the center of gravity of the vehicle are as close as possible (L is short).
Adjust the height of the lift pads so that the vehicle is level and the pads do not contact the rocker molding, and securely align the grooves of the lift pads with the rigid rack support positions.
Always lock the swing arms before working.
Lift up the vehicle until the tires are slightly off the ground, rock the vehicle and check that it is stable.

step1.ptxt: Precautions when Using 4-post Lift and Drive-on Type Lift

step2.ptxt: Follow the lift instruction manual and work safely.
Do not damage the tires and wheels with the free wheel beam.
Secure the vehicle using wheel chocks.
